title: Across the Thread Boundary: What a Queued Connection Actually Does

questions.question: A signal is emitted on a worker thread and its slot belongs to an object on the main thread. With Qt's default connection, where does the slot run?
options: On the main thread, because the argument is copied and posted to the receiver's event loop
On whichever thread is idle
On a thread Qt creates for the purpose
On the worker thread, immediately, like any function call
questions.explanation: AutoConnection decides at emit time: same thread is a direct call, different threads is a queued delivery. That is how a widget can be updated from data that arrived somewhere else without ever being touched from there.

questions.question: What does Qt::DirectConnection do across a thread boundary?
options: Refuses to connect
Behaves the same as AutoConnection
Runs the slot on the emitting thread, so the receiver's members are touched from the wrong place
Blocks the emitter until the receiver has run the slot
questions.explanation: For a widget that is undefined behaviour rather than a race to reason about, and it usually works, which is why it survives to production.

questions.question: connect returns true and the slot never runs. What is the most likely reason?
options: A queued connection cannot copy the argument type, so every delivery is dropped with one line on the console
The connection type was wrong
The receiver was destroyed
The signal was never emitted
questions.explanation: connect returning true means the signatures matched, not that anything will arrive. Measured, a signal carrying Qt::HANDLE delivered zero of a hundred, and the program had no way to see the warning.

questions.question: On Qt 6, does a plain struct need qRegisterMetaType to cross a queued connection?
options: Only if it contains pointers
Only when the receiver is a widget
No: measured, five hundred of five hundred arrive with no registration at all, because the function pointer syntax registers the type
Yes, always, as on Qt 5
questions.explanation: Which matters because the obsolete advice hides the real hazard. The types that still fail are ones recorded under a name Qt cannot resolve, such as a typedef, and they fail silently.

questions.question: The worker has finished producing and the log has received nothing. The receiver's event loop has not run. What happened to the readings?
options: The emit blocked until the loop ran
They were dropped, since there was nobody to receive them
They were delivered directly, bypassing the loop
They are waiting as posted events, and arrive as soon as the loop runs
questions.explanation: Which is the shape of a great many bugs that present as a dead sensor. The data is neither lost nor received.

questions.question: What decides which thread an object's slots run on?
options: The connection type alone
The object's own thread affinity, set by moveToThread, independent of any connection
The thread that created the connection
The thread that owns the sender
questions.explanation: Affinity belongs to the object. Neither object in a connection has to be told about the other's thread, which is what makes the pattern compose.
